REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. ____ No. D ____ S. 2, Sp. Br. Date ____ April __, 1933.）

Subject (in full) Case against Zung Zai Woo (陳瑞和) - extradited to Chinese Authorities for communist activities.

Made by ____ and ____ Forwarded by D. I. Ross

Regarding the endorsement of the Officer i/c Special Branch of April 21, 1933 on the attached file, I have to report that D.S.I. Golder, while inadvertently omitting to notify D.S. Hide to have the accused placed on a Writ of Detention, informed him (D.S. Hide) that if he had any doubt as to the correctness of the procedure to be followed, to ring up D.I. Ross when the case went to Court the following morning for further instructions. In accordance with this arrangement D.S. Hide telephoned D.I. Ross during the forenoon of April 20, but owing to some misunderstanding which unfortunately I am unable to explain, I understood him to say that the case had already been concluded and that the prisoner had been extradited to the Chinese Authorities.

On making further enquiries I ascertained that the Public Safety Bureau had apparently established a prima facie case and in view of the fact that the accused did not claim to be a resident of the Settlement and admitted being in the pay of the Chinese Communist Party, it was deemed useless to pursue the matter further.

Misunderstandings of this nature in future would doubtless be obviated if copies of the memo of the Officer i/c Special Branch of March 6, 1933 (copy attached) were distributed to all stations.

主题（全称） 针对 Zung Zai Woo (陳瑞和) 的案件 - 因共产主义活动被引渡至中国当局。

由 ____ 和 ____ 制作 由 D. I. Ross 转呈

关于附卷中特别科主管警官于1933年4月21日的批注，本人须报告称，副督察 Golder 在无意中未通知巡官 Hide 对被告签发拘留令，但告知他（巡官 Hide），如果他对应遵循的程序是否正确存有任何疑虑，可在次日上午案件开庭时致电督察 Ross 以获取进一步指示。根据这一安排，巡官 Hide 于4月20日上午致电督察 Ross，但由于某种不幸无法解释的误解，我理解他说案件已经结案，且囚犯已被引渡至中国当局。

经进一步查询，我查明公共安全局显然已确立了初步证据，鉴于被告并未声称是租界居民，并承认受雇于中国共产党，认为继续追究此事已无必要。

Charge Application for handing over to the Public Safety Bureau.
Application is hereby made for the above described person, who was arrested at 10.20 p.m. on the 19/4/33, at 21 Doong Shing Lee, off Kinchow Road, to be handed over to the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau by whom he is wanted for having been concerned in activities of a communistic nature.

DISTRICT COURT High court

Proceed-ings
Mr, T.S. Lea appeared for the police.
Mr, Lea:- The accused was arrested at the request of the S.P.S.B. by police attached to Yulin Rd, police station on a S.S.D. court warrant, at 10.20.p.m. on the 19/4/33 at No, 21 Doong Shing Li off Kinchow Rd. Accused gave his name as Sung Ching Tser(alias) Lau Zung. Under a used's bed was discovered a Mimeograph & a quantity of communistic literature, also an list of addresses, as follows, 1857 Ferry Rd, 59 Zung Yui Li off Tiendong Rd, and 238 Maxwell Rd. When questioned accused denied that he was a member of the communistic party, but stated that two of his friends were, names, Zung and another. A man named Sung Ming Ching in custody of the S.P.S.B. can testify to the effect that accused is a communist, and is in court this afternoon.

诉讼程序
T.S. Lea 先生代表警方出庭。

Accused:- I live at 21 Doong Sning Li, and occupy the whole
of the upstairs. I used to live on Woochang Rd, The mimeograph
machine was sent to my place by one named, Zu g and the literature
and books by one named Wong. In the Chinese New year I met a man
named Yang in the Public gardens, and I told him that I had no
work, so he said that he would give me a job of writing, and that he
would pay me $10.00. I had not written anything yet. The original
papers were sent to me on the 4/4/33 for me to copy. They were
sent by Wong & Zung, but they did not say whether it was for
compiling a magazine or only pamphlets.

Judge handing accused a paper:- Did you write this?.

Accused:- "Yes" on the 20/4/33 .

Wit, Sung Ming Ching :- My age is 39 years & I am a native of
Kompo. I used to work in a cotton mill and formerly resided at
No 37 Tsu Tuh Li Penang Rd, and was arrested on the 18/4/33 . I also
had interests in a labour union for the cotton factory, and I know
that some of the communists joined the union. I know the accused
as I was introduced to him by a man named Zung. I met him first in
the Public Gardens, and Tsang introduced him to me. I gave him some
information about the factory to put into print. I have also given
him facts about strikes and workers being dismissed, but he has not
printed them for me yet. Accused also got information from other
factories. The property belongs to a man who is in custody of the
Tser Kai Jau, P.S.B. I heard that his name was Lieu. I have been to
accused's house on two occasions to make arrangements about print-
ing the news. After he got the information he used to print the
pamphlets which were spread amongst the workers. I dont know whether
this accused has joined the C.P.C. but I know he has the Labour
union, and I am a clerk in it. Accused is also the editor of a

缴获的共产主义文献及印刷设备。我请求将被告移交我方当局进行进一步审讯。

被告：- 我住在同兴里21号，占据整个楼上。我以前住在武昌路。油印机是一个叫 Zu g 的人送到我这儿的，文献和书籍是一个叫 Wong 的人送来的。春节期间，我在公共花园遇到一个叫 Yang 的人，我告诉他我没有工作，他说会给我一份抄写的工作，并支付我10.00美元。我还没有写过任何东西。原始文件是1933年4月4日寄给我的，让我抄写。它们是由 Wong 和 Zung 寄来的，但他们没说这是为了编纂杂志还是仅仅印制小册子。

法官递给被告一张纸：- 这是你写的吗？

被告：- “是的”，1933年4月20日。

证人 Sung Ming Ching：- 我今年39岁，籍贯 Kompo（音译）。我曾在一家棉纺厂工作，以前住在槟榔路祖德里37号，于1933年4月18日被捕。我也在棉纺厂工会中有利益关系，我知道一些共产党员加入了工会。我认识被告，因为是一个叫 Zung 的人把我介绍给他的。我第一次在公共花园见到他，Tsang 把他介绍给我。我给他提供了一些关于工厂的信息以供印刷。我还向他提供了关于罢工和工人被解雇的事实，但他尚未为我印刷。被告也从其他工厂获取信息。这些财产属于一个由 Tser Kai Jau（音译，上海公共安全局）羁押的人。我听说他的名字叫 Lieu。我曾两次去被告家安排印刷新闻事宜。他拿到信息后，就会印刷小册子并在工人中散发。我不知道这名被告是否加入了中国共产党，但我知道他在工会中，我是工会的一名职员。被告也是一份小报的编辑。

Zung Zai Wo (陳瑞和) alias Lau Zung (老陳).
Hai-Ien Hsien (海鹽), Chekiang.           D.S. Pitts.
Yulin Rd. St.      20th. April, 1933             Clerk Chang.

My name is Zung Zai Wo, alias Lau Zung, aged 30, married,
native of Hai-Ien Hsien, Chekiang Province, at present unemployed.
    I first studied in my native place under the tuition of
my father who was a school teacher, until I was fifteen years
of age.    I then entered a primary school in my native place
where I studied until I was eighteen, after which I went to
Kashing and entered the Middle School there, remaining for two
years.
    After this I came to Shanghai bearing a letter of recom-
mendation from a relative named Tsang Kyi Zung (張季良) to
a man named Tsang Kyeu Sung (張菊生), a former director
of the The Commercial Press.    Through the latter I was enabled
to obtain a position at the Commercial Press as a proof reader
at $14 per month.    This was in 1924.    I remained with this
company until the factory was destroyed during the local Sino-
Japanese hostilities in the early part of 1932.    At that time
I was receiving $39.50 per month and still retained my pos-
ition as a proof reader.
    During my employment with this concern I first lived at
Zung Tah Li (順泰里), Pau Tung Road (寶通路) Chapei
until 1926, when I removed to Zung Zung Li (順成里),
Chung Hwa Sing (中華新路) Road, Chapei.    I lived at this
address until 1928 when I got married and removed again to
No. 5 Nyeen Nyeen Li (元元里), Tientungan Road, Chapei.
I lived at this address until the commencement of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities, when I returned for safety's sake to my
native place with my wife and two children.    I remained there
page_data.zh:
Zung Zai Wo (陳瑞和)，别名 Lau Zung (老陳)。
浙江省海盐县。           警佐 Pitts。
榆林路捕房      1933年4月20日             书记员 Chang。

我叫 Zung Zai Wo，别名 Lau Zung，30岁，已婚，
籍贯浙江省海盐县，目前无业。
    我早年在家乡由担任教师的父亲教导读书，
直到十五岁。随后进入家乡的一所小学就读，
直至十八岁，之后前往嘉兴，进入那里的中学，
读了两年。
    此后我携带亲戚 Tsang Kyi Zung (張季良) 的推荐信
来到上海，去见一位名叫 Tsang Kyeu Sung (張菊生) 的人，
他是商务印书馆的前任董事。通过后者，我得以在商务印书馆
获得一份校对员的职位，月薪14美元。那是1924年。
我一直在这家公司工作，直到1932年初当地中日冲突期间
工厂被毁。当时我的月薪为39.50美元，仍保留着
校对员的职位。
    在这家公司任职期间，我起初住在闸北宝通路顺泰里，
直到1926年，搬至闸北中华新路顺成里。
我住在这个地址直到1928年结婚，再次搬至闸北天通庵路
元元里5号。我住在这个地址直到中日冲突爆发，
为了安全起见，我带着妻子和两个孩子返回家乡。我留在那里

page_data.en:
- 2 -

doing nothing until January 1933 when I returned to Shanghai,
having learned that the Commercial Press had recommenced bus-
iness. It was my intention to rejoin the company.
Arriving here I put up at a country house on Bubbling Well
Road near Great Western Road - the residence of my relative
Wang Oo Zaung (王和尚). I stayed there for some five
days only. Whilst still residing at this address, I vis-
ited the Bund Public Gardens on January 29 and accidentally
met one named Yang Nyih S (楊宜思), who formerly worked
with me at the The Commercial Press. He told me he was living
at 238 Maxwell Road. I asked him if he could find me a job
as I was still unemployed. He agreed to introduce me to
two men who would assist me and told me to meet them at
the entrance to Sincere's Departmental Stores on Naking Road
on February 4, 1933.
After my meeting with Yang I rented a room at an unnum-
bered house on Woochang Road. On February 4, I met the
two men whom Yang had described to me. I knew them as
Wong (王) and Zang (陳). I met them several times
and on March 28, I removed to my present address at 21 Dong
Sing Li (同兴里), Kwaming Road. After several talks
with these two individuals who told me that they were cotton
brokers, they agreed to pay me $10 per month for copying and
duplicating various tracts of literature which they would hand
to me diverse times. On April 4, they sent two myriograph
duplicators to my address for the purpose of printing the
aforementioned writings, but I told them I did not know how
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

无所事事，直到1933年1月，得知商务印书馆已恢复营业，
我便回到上海。我打算重新加入该公司。
抵达这里后，我借住在静安寺路近大西路的一处乡间住宅——
我的亲戚 Wang Oo Zaung (王和尚) 的住所。我只在那里
住了大约五天。仍住在此处期间，我于1月29日
游览外滩公园，偶然遇到一位名叫 Yang Nyih S (楊宜思) 的人，
他以前和我一起在商务印书馆工作。他告诉我他住在麦克斯韦尔路238号。
我问他能否帮我找份工作，因为我仍然失业。他同意
将我介绍给两位能协助我的人，并让我于1933年2月4日
在南京路先施公司百货商店门口与他们见面。
与 Yang 会面后，我在武昌路一所无门牌号的房子里租了一间房。
2月4日，我见到了 Yang 向我描述的那两个人。我知道他们叫
Wong (王) 和 Zang (陳)。我与他们会面数次，
并于3月28日搬至目前的住址：昆明路同兴里21号。
在与这两个人多次交谈后，他们告诉我他们是棉花经纪人，
他们同意每月支付我10美元，用于抄写和复印他们
不时交给我的各种文宣品。4月4日，他们送了两台
油印机到我的住址，目的是印刷前述文字，但我告诉他们我不知道如何

page_data.en:
- 3 -

to use these machines. They told me to leave the machines
at my home and they would show me how to manipulate them when
necessary. However, they brought no literature for me to
copy and I have never done anywork at all for them and they
have never handed me any money.

I do not know where these two men are living but their
descriptions are as follows:

WONG. Native of Chingkiang; aged about 28; height about 5'5";
round face; fair complexion; cropped hair; no glasses;
wears Chinese clothing; appears to be of the merchant
class and seems to be very respectable.

ZUNG. Native of Soochow; aged about 32; height about 5'7";
long face; fair complexion; long hair parted in the
middle; wears Chinese clothing; appears to be of the
merchant class and seems quite respectable.

I am not a communist and am not a member of any party. I
have never been arrested before and have never been approached
by anyone regarding matters appertaining to radical thought. I
personally am not interested in politics at all.

This is my true statement/

Signed : Zung Zai Wo.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

使用这些机器。他们让我把机器留在家中，
必要时他们会来教我如何操作。然而，他们并未带来任何
供我抄写的文宣品，我也从未为他们做过任何工作，
他们也从未给过我任何钱。

我不知道这两个人住在哪里，但他们的体貌特征如下：

WONG。镇江籍；约28岁；身高约5英尺5英寸；
圆脸；肤色白皙；短发；不戴眼镜；
穿中式服装；看似商人阶层，显得非常正派。

ZUNG。苏州籍；约32岁；身高约5英尺7英寸；
长脸；肤色白皙；长发中分；穿中式服装；
看似商人阶层，显得相当正派。

我不是共产党员，也不是任何党派的成员。
我以前从未被捕过，也从未有人就激进思想相关事宜
接触过我。我个人对政治完全不感兴趣。

这是我的真实供词/

签名：Zung Zai Wo。
